# 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council Election

## Overview

The 2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election was held on **3 May 2012**, the same day as other local elections across England. One-third of the council seats were up for election, as is typical for metropolitan boroughs that hold elections in thirds.

## Political Context

- This election took place during the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government nationally
- The Liberal Democrats had historically been strong in Stockport
- Labour was seeking to make gains following the national swing against the coalition parties

## Results

**Labour** made significant gains in this election, reflecting broader national trends of dissatisfaction with the coalition government, particularly the Liberal Democrats.

The **Liberal Democrats** suffered losses, consistent with their declining support nationally following their entry into coalition with the Conservatives.

## Council Composition

Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council consists of **63 councillors** representing 21 wards (3 councillors per ward).

## Significance

This election was part of a period of political change in Stockport, as Labour strengthened its position on the council at the expense of the Liberal Democrats, who had previously been the dominant force in local politics.
